title: Feedback, Questions & Reflection
whatItIs: The standard asks instructors to give formative feedback, answer questions and help learners reflect. Part 3 and the standards check mark all three.
keyFacts: Feedback should be relevant, positive and honest, never giving a false sense of ability.
Where possible, put a weakness as a learning opportunity; if something is dangerous, say so plainly.
Feedback is two-way, ideally prompted by the pupil; their feedback, especially how they felt, is never ignored.
Deal with the pupil's questions as soon as possible, or point them to a suitable source.
End of lesson: encourage the pupil to reflect; give a balanced overview of strengths and weaknesses if they don't.
Instructors reflect too: unit 5 asks for a reflective log and getting feedback in a non-defensive way.

items.title: Stop safely
items.text: Find a safe place to examine the incident, soon after.

items.title: Let the pupil speak
items.text: Give them time to express any fears or concerns the incident caused.

items.title: Reflect together
items.text: Support them to reflect; clarify what they missed.

items.title: Agree a strategy
items.text: Find strategies for next time; check they can use them.

a.label: Closed questions
points: Of little use otherwise with a highly able pupil

b.label: Open questions
points: May confuse a struggling pupil of limited ability
Match any question to the pupil's level of ability

onTheTest.question: To end a lesson, an instructor only asks 'what score would you give yourself?'. How does DVSA see this?
options: Meaningless on its own: a development need
Required at the end of every part 3
Only suitable for full licence holders
onTheTest.why: Examiner guidance 3.24: simply asking this is meaningless and shows a development need for the instructor.

onTheTest.question: A keen pupil keeps asking questions near a busy junction. Best response?
options: Hold them: focus on the hazard, answer when stopped
Answer each one fully straight away
Ignore them until the next lesson
onTheTest.why: Examiner guidance 3.24: manage the keenness without demotivating: hold the questions, focus on the hazard, stop later to cover them.

traps: Non-stop feedback, even accurate, can demotivate or be dangerous: silence can be powerful feedback.
Accepting a pupil's glowing self-assessment when there were risks isn't acceptable: honesty is key.
Feedback given long after an incident doesn't help: the pupil can't link it to what happened.
Refusing to hear reasonable feedback on your own performance shows a lack of competence.
